deduped_items.body_text:
El enorme salto de Primaria a la ESO en Córdoba: «Para ellos puede suponer un mundo, pero en pocas semanas ya se han adaptado»
Los centros llevan a cabo algunas acciones de acompañamiento temprano para suavizar la llegada de los adolescentes a las nuevas aulas
Córdoba
«¿Qué día es hoy? Martes, 15 de septiembre. Apúntalo bien en la agenda porque hoy es el día en el que vuestra vida cambia». La frase retumba en una tímida clase de 1º de ESO del IES Luis de Góngora. Es martes ... y, para sus alumnos, comienza algo más que un nuevo curso escolar. Para muchos de ellos es su primer día en un instituto, el inicio de una etapa que supone dejar atrás el colegio y enfrentarse a un escenario completamente nuevo.
Este martes han comenzado un nuevo curso escolar en Córdoba más de 75.500 estudiantes de Secundaria, Bachillerato y Formación Profesional. Para muchos, el regreso a las aulas supone simplemente continuar un año más junto a los compañeros que ya conocen. Para otros, sin embargo, significa un cambio importante en su vida académica y personal.
El salto de Primaria a Secundaria y verse por primera vez en un instituto es uno de los principales retos que afrontan alumnos y familias. Nuevos profesores, nuevas instalaciones, más horas lectivas y un temario mucho más exigente que el que han tenido hasta ahora conforman el escenario al que tienen que adaptarse los estudiantes que comienzan 1º de ESO.
Noticia relacionada
Para hacer de esa transición algo más dulce, los centros educativos de Córdoba toman distintas medidas para facilitar la adaptación de los alumnos a lo que será su nuevo centro durante los próximos cuatro años. En el IES Fidiana llevan a cabo un «programa de tránsito» para gestionar ese paso de Primaria a Secundaria. Su directora, María Ángeles Domínguez, explica que el proceso comienza mucho antes de que los alumnos crucen por primera vez las puertas del instituto.
«Empezamos este curso y ya estamos casi pensando en el año que viene. Empezamos a tener reuniones ya en enero con los colegios adscritos y, a partir de ahí, planificamos todo», señala. Una de las acciones consiste en que el alumnado conozca previamente el centro al que acudirá el curso siguiente. «El alumnado viene a conocer el centro y también hay otro día en el que alumnos de sexto de Primaria vienen a pasar un día. Son los alumnos 'embajadores'. Vienen a una clase de Primero, van a su centro y lo cuentan allí», explica Domínguez.
La familiarización no se limita a los estudiantes. Las familias también tienen la oportunidad de conocer las instalaciones y resolver sus dudas antes del comienzo del curso. «Tenemos también una reunión con los padres, se les enseña todo el centro. Vienen también los alumnos con ellos», apunta.
Suavizar el cambio
El objetivo es que el cambio no resulte tan brusco. La directora reconoce que «imagino que para ellos tiene que ser un mundo», aunque la adaptación suele producirse rápidamente. «En un par de semanas están completamente ya habituados, conocen las rutinas del centro y la verdad que además aquí se les cuida mucho a los de Primero», señala. El tránsito tampoco se trabaja únicamente desde la perspectiva del alumnado. Los centros coordinan también el trabajo de los profesores para tratar de evitar que el cambio de etapa tenga un impacto académico negativo.
«Y no solamente a nivel del alumnado, sino que se valoran los profesores de allí por los departamentos», explica Domínguez. La coordinación permite poner en común «lo que estáis dando allí, qué es lo que vamos a dar aquí, qué se les va a exigir y qué es lo que tienen que ver allí para que luego se pueda ver aquí».
La intención es que los contenidos trabajados en sexto de Primaria sirvan como punto de partida para los que encontrarán los alumnos en Primero de ESO y que no exista un salto académico demasiado acusado. «No se nota un impacto académico», señala la directora. Y pone como ejemplo las matemáticas: «Se ponen de acuerdo los departamentos para ver qué contenidos se impart

deduped_items.body_text:
Real Madrid
El anotador de los Lakers Nick Smith Jr. se autopresenta como nuevo fichaje del Real Madrid
El escolta estadounidense pondrá fin a una búsqueda de varios meses por un anotador puro en el perímetro para completar la plantilla dirigida por Pedro Martínez
Pablo Sierra
Madrid
Nick Smith Jr. no ha esperado al Real Madrid. El escolta americano publicó el pasado sábado una foto vistiendo la camiseta madridista: a expensas de que el club oficialice su incorporación, se convertirá en el séptimo refuerzo del verano para el nuevo proyecto ... de Pedro Martínez y firmará por una temporada, hasta el final del curso 2026-2027.
Smith Jr., nacido el 18 de abril de 2004 en Jacksonville (Arkansas), llega como agente libre tras no encontrar acomodo en la NBA para esta temporada. Con su 1,88 de estatura, fue elegido en el puesto 27 de la primera ronda del draft de 2023 por Charlotte Hornets, equipo en el que disputó sus dos primeras temporadas en la NBA antes de firmar con Los Angeles Lakers el pasado verano. Su fichaje por el conjunto blanco supone su primera experiencia baloncestística fuera de Estados Unidos.
El escolta desembarca en el baloncesto europeo tras firmar una media de 7,6 puntos a lo largo de sus tres campañas en la NBA. Durante este ciclo, el estadounidense también ha dejado huella en la G-League —la liga de desarrollo de la NBA—, competición en la que ha exhibido su versión más explosiva y desequilibrante con unos promedios estelares de 20,5 puntos y 5,2 asistencias por partido.
Noticia relacionada
- 
Baloncesto Pablo Sierra
Su llegada cierra, además, una búsqueda que el club llevaba meses con el objetivo sobre la mesa: la de un anotador exterior puro, capaz de generar tiro por sí mismo en el perímetro. Antes de Smith Jr., nombres como Nadir Hifi, Lester Quiñones, Armoni Brooks o incluso Jean Montero habían sido vinculados al club madridista.
El base dominicano, entrenado precisamente por Pedro Martínez en Valencia Basket, era uno de los nombres que se rumoreaba para reforzar al Real Madrid. Montero venía de firmar una temporada de ensueño —18,6 puntos, 4,2 rebotes y 5,8 asistencias de media en los playoffs de Euroliga— que llevó al Valencia hasta su primera Final Four de la competición y le valió el MVP de las finales de la Liga Endesa. Pero el Olympiacos, precisamente el equipo que apeó al Real Madrid en la final de la pasada Euroliga, se adelantó en la negociación y anunció su fichaje por tres temporadas el pasado mes de mayo.
Smith Jr. y Montero comparten vocación anotadora, pero responden a realidades distintas: mientras el dominicano es un generador de juego con capacidad de mando de partido ya contrastada en la élite europea, el estadounidense llega como una apuesta más arriesgada dada su nula experiencia fuera de Estados Unidos, pero con el potencial suficiente como para convertirse en uno de los anotadores más letales de Europa.
La salida de Ndiaye y una plantilla reconstruida a 3 días de la Supercopa de Europa
El fichaje de Smith Jr. llega para completar una reconstrucción casi integral de la plantilla de la mano de Juan Carlos Sánchez. El, de nuevo, director técnico ha contado hasta ahora con siete incorporaciones: Pradilla, Luwawu-Cabarrot, Jantunen, Shulga, Sarr, Jones y Eli John Ndiaye, canterano recuperado este verano desde los Atlanta Hawks mediante el derecho de tanteo, con el que el club superó una oferta del Valencia.
Precisamente Ndiaye ha protagonizado el último movimiento antes de Smith Jr.: el pasado 11 de septiembre, el Real Madrid oficializó su cesión al Asisa Joventut para el resto de la temporada, una salida motivada por la saturación de efectivos en el puesto de interior y las lesiones que lastraron al joven Eli, que deberá jugar asiduamente para recuperar su mejor versión.
Con la gira de pretemporada ya cerrada —tres victorias y una derrota, incluido el séptimo entorchado del Torneo Costa del Sol tras arrollar al Unicaja en la final—, el conjunto de Pedro Martínez afronta ahora su primer t

deduped_items.body_text:
Miguel Dalmau, premio de Novela Café Gijón por 'La reina de Cuba'
El Jurado destaca que es «una fascinante geografía literaria que se mueve entre la Cuba prerrevolucionaria y la España de la posguerra»
Madrid
El jurado del premio Café Gijón, que convoca el Ayuntamiento de Gijón, ha premiado, en su 76ª edición, la novela 'La reina de Cuba', de Miguel Dalmau. En su fallo, el jurado ha destacado que se trata de una obra de ... un «estilo ágil, torrencial y llena de autenticidad (…). Una fascinante geografía literaria que se mueve entre la Cuba prerrevolucionaria y la España de la posguerra». El galardón, dotado con 20.000 euros, ha contado con un jurado compuesto por Pilar Adón, Ricardo Menéndez Salmón, Gioconda Belli, Marcos Giralt Torrente y Mercedes Monmany, en calidad de presidenta.
'La reina de Cuba' no solo es un emocionante homenaje a las mujeres de la posguerra. Es también el retrato de una mujer apasionada y singular que jamás permitió que la llama de la isla de Cuba se apagara en su corazón.
Miguel Dalmau inició los estudios de Medicina, que interrumpiría para dedicarse de lleno a la escritura. Entre su labor como novelista se encuentran las obras 'La grieta' (1998), 'El reloj de Hitler' (premio de Novela Breve Juan March Cencillo), 'La noche del diablo' (2009), '¡Quiero vivir en América!' (2020) y 'Las cenizas de Berta' (premio Internacional de Novela Ciudad de Barbastro 2025). Además, es autor de las celebradas biografías 'Los Goytisolo' (1999, finalista del premio Anagrama de Ensayo), 'La balada de Oscar Wilde' (2000), 'Jaime Gil de Biedma' (2004, 2026), que fue llevada al cine, 'Julio Cortázar' (2015) o 'Pasolini' (premio Comillas de Historia, Biografía y Memorias 2022). Y del ensayo 'El ocaso del pudor' (2012). Ediciones Siruela publicará la novela el próximo mes de enero.

deduped_items.title: From left to right on the political spectrum, voters would tax wealth over wages
deduped_items.summary: Voters from across the political spectrum, including those on the right, are more positive about the wealth tax than the Tweede Kamer parties, according to research by Kieskompas commissioned by Tr
deduped_items.body_text:
From left to right on the political spectrum, voters would tax wealth over wages
Voters from across the political spectrum, including those on the right, are more positive about the wealth tax than the Tweede Kamer parties, according to research by Kieskompas commissioned by Trouw.
The sentiment is also present on the right. Half of VVD voters find raising wealth tax acceptable provided the tax on income does not follow. Inside the coalition government, VVD is blocking D66’s and CDA’s desire to levy more tax on wealth.
Conflict over wealth in Box 3 is ongoing, and the coalition will have to resolve it in the next months. According to leaked budget day documents, Trouw said the cabinet is allegedly set to raise the payroll tax.
A clear majority of the 4,600 Kieskpmpas survey respondents also support limiting the mortgage-interest deduction or raising inheritance tax. This is, once again, especially true if payroll tax does not have to rise as well.
According to the data, 54 percent of VVD voters favor getting rid of or gradually phasing out the mortgage-interest deduction, while 44 percent are against it.
Among the D66 voters, 69 percent support the deduction being scaled back or stopped. This is the same of 62 percent of the surveyed CDA voters.

deduped_items.title: Three Men Sentenced in Catania Sexual Assault Case Involving Hungarian Tourists
deduped_items.summary: The Criminal Court of Catania sentenced two Moroccan men to 7 years and 2 months in prison each for the sexual assault of two Hungarian female tourists in Sicily last year, and their third accomplice to 7 years and 4 months—the first-instance verdict was handed down on Monday. The men, aged 23 to 26, were […] The post Three Men Sentenced in Catania Sexual Assault Case Involving Hungarian Tourists appeared first on Hungary Today.
deduped_items.body_text:
Italian prosecutor vows full justice as suspects face group sexual violence charges; case cracked thanks to victim’s quick-thinking sister and phone tracker.Continue reading
The Criminal Court of Catania sentenced two Moroccan men to 7 years and 2 months in prison each for the sexual assault of two Hungarian female tourists in Sicily last year, and their third accomplice to 7 years and 4 months—the first-instance verdict was handed down on Monday.
The men, aged 23 to 26, were convicted of sexual assault by multiple perpetrators, as well as drug possession and forcing the victims to use drugs. The case was tried under expedited proceedings, so one-third of the original potential sentence was waived. Marof Hamza and Arsab Marvan each received seven years and two months in prison, while Barsan Szufian received seven years and four months.
Since their arrest last year, the perpetrators have been held separately in different Italian prisons.
They were present when the verdict was read, but were not given the opportunity to speak after the court’s decision was announced.
At the time of the crime, all three Moroccan nationals were in Italy as illegal immigrants; however, they were not sentenced for this offense in this proceeding.
The court will issue a separate ruling on the compensation to be awarded to the women. The Italian state fund established for victims of violence will also contribute to the amount.
Massimiliano Scaringella, the attorney representing the two Hungarian women, told MTI that he is satisfied because “this is a significant ruling that reaffirmed that such things cannot happen in Italy. Such behavior cannot be tolerated and will not be accepted. The court found the accounts of the young women who suffered the assault to be entirely credible.”
The two women did not attend the hearings. Massimiliano Scaringella emphasized that the victims had experienced trauma and wished to remain absent to protect their privacy.

deduped_items.body_text:
Prague Has the Most Unaffordable Rents for Minimum-Wage Earners in the EU
Prague Morning
Prague has the highest rent-to-minimum-wage ratio among EU capitals, with the average two-bedroom apartment costing 185% of the gross minimum wage.
Prague has become the European Union’s least affordable capital for minimum-wage earners looking to rent a home, according to a new analysis by the European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC).
The average monthly rent for a two-bedroom apartment in the Czech capital reaches €1,710, compared with a gross monthly minimum wage of €924. This means rent alone amounts to 185% of the minimum wage.
Lisbon follows in second place, with rent accounting for 168% of the gross minimum wage. Budapest ranks third at 159%, followed by Bratislava at 158%.
Other capitals where average rent exceeds the gross minimum wage include Sofia (154%), Athens (153%), and Riga (151%).
The figures highlight the pressure facing minimum-wage earners in cities where housing costs have risen significantly faster than incomes.
How Prague Compares with Western Europe
Prague’s position is particularly striking when compared with several Western European capitals.
In Paris, average rent accounts for 138% of the gross minimum wage, while the figure stands at 125% in Madrid and 113% in Dublin.
At the other end of the ranking, Brussels is the most affordable capital for minimum-wage earners in the comparison. Average rent there represents 70% of the gross minimum wage. Berlin follows at 76%, while the figure is 85% in Nicosia and 87% in Luxembourg.
Housing Costs Across the EU
According to Eurostat’s latest figures cited in the analysis, housing and utility bills account for 23.6% of household spending across the European Union.
The ETUC has called for stronger collective bargaining, greater consideration of housing costs when setting minimum wages, and increased investment in social housing.
The organisation also noted that rents can be more affordable when measured against national minimum wages rather than those in capital cities. Among the 16 EU countries analysed, the share of the gross minimum wage required for rent ranged from 33% in Poland to 61% in Malta.

deduped_items.body_text:
Nearly 40 Percent of Young Czechs Experience Financial Stress Every Month
Prague Morning
Money worries affect almost one in three Czech adults, but younger people are facing a greater burden.
A new survey found that 39 percent of people aged 18 to 26 experience financial anxiety at least once a month, with household income playing a major role in how people feel about their finances.
Financial concerns are common across the Czech Republic. According to a survey conducted by Ipsos for Home Credit, 28 percent of adults experience worries about money at least once a month. Another 35 percent report financial stress several times a year.
Young adults face the greatest pressure
People aged 18 to 26 are the most likely to experience regular financial stress. Nearly four in ten respondents in this age group said they worry about money at least once a month.
Home Credit attributed the pressure partly to the cost of housing and everyday expenses. For young adults trying to establish themselves financially, rising prices in recent years have made it harder to absorb unexpected costs.
An unplanned bill or other expense can therefore create a serious problem, particularly for those who have limited savings.
Household income makes a significant difference
The survey found a clear relationship between household income and financial anxiety.
Among households earning up to CZK 40,000 per month, 41 percent of respondents reported experiencing financial stress. The proportion decreases as household income rises.
People living in households with monthly incomes above CZK 70,000 reported the lowest levels of financial concern.
Age and education also appear to influence how people view their finances. Respondents aged 54 to 65 and university students reported lower levels of stress than some other groups. In both categories, 43 percent said they did not experience financial stress at all.
Financial stress may also affect physical health
The consequences of financial difficulties can extend beyond anxiety and everyday worries.
The material also refers to research published by the American Mayo Clinic in 2025. According to the research cited, long-term financial distress and food insecurity may be associated with poorer cardiovascular health and a higher risk of death.
The findings underline the potential connection between financial security and overall well-being. However, the Czech survey does not establish whether financial stress directly causes health problems.
The survey was conducted by Ipsos in June 2026 among 1,026 people.

deduped_items.title: Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
deduped_items.summary: Following Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla's announcement that Harry Roque's asylum bid in Europe has been denied, Malacañang said the former spokesperson's political persecution claims were baseless.
deduped_items.body_text:
Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang said on Tuesday, September 15, that the asylum request and political persecution claims of former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque lacked basis as he continues to face charges in the Philippines.
According to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro, during a press briefing, aside from qualified human trafficking complaints, Roque also faces accusations of land grabbing and tax evasion.
“Ang paniniwala ng PCO (Presidential Communications Office) ay wala pong batayan ang ginawang request ni Harry Roque na sinasabing political persecution lang ang ginagawa sa kanya. Maliwanag naman po ang mga kaso, hindi lang qualified human trafficking,” Castro said.
(The PCO believes that Harry Roque’s request claiming he’s experiencing political persecution has no basis. The cases are clear, and they involve not only qualified human trafficking.)
The Palace’s comment came after Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said in a separate press briefing earlier Tuesday that Roque’s asylum request had been denied.
Remulla previously said Roque was applying for asylum in Austria, citing political persecution.
In the Philippines, Roque faces non-bailable qualified human trafficking charges filed by the Department of Justice over his alleged active participation in the operations of Lucky South 99, the illegal Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) hub in Pampanga, which was raided in 2024.
An arrest warrant was issued by a Pampanga court against Roque and his co-accused in May 2025 for the qualified human trafficking case.
Meanwhile, in March this year, a group of farmers from Bataan filed land-grabbing complaints against Roque for allegedly transferring land titles, which were supposed to be distributed to 100 farmers, to a private corporation connected to a POGO firm.
The corporation's listed address supposedly pointed to Roque’s office.
The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) also filed a tax evasion case against Roque and his wife in April this year for allegedly failing to pay P3.35 million in taxes connected to transactions involving Biancham Holdings and Trading Inc.
Roque denied all accusations, saying these are all part of the continuous political attacks against him.
He also dismissed Remulla’s claim that his asylum request had been denied, calling it “fake news.”
Roque, who served as the Palace spokesperson under then-President Rodrigo Duterte, left the Philippines in 2024.

deduped_items.title: Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
deduped_items.summary: Following Interior Secretary Jonvic Remulla's announcement that Harry Roque's asylum bid in Europe has been denied, Malacañang said the former spokesperson's political persecution claims were baseless.
deduped_items.body_text:
Palace: Roque’s asylum bid, persecution claims lack basis
MANILA, Philippines — Malacañang said on Tuesday, September 15, that the asylum request and political persecution claims of former presidential spokesperson Harry Roque lacked basis as he continues to face charges in the Philippines.
According to Palace Press Officer Claire Castro, during a press briefing, aside from qualified human trafficking complaints, Roque also faces accusations of land grabbing and tax evasion.
“Ang paniniwala ng PCO (Presidential Communications Office) ay wala pong batayan ang ginawang request ni Harry Roque na sinasabing political persecution lang ang ginagawa sa kanya. Maliwanag naman po ang mga kaso, hindi lang qualified human trafficking,” Castro said.
(The PCO believes that Harry Roque’s request claiming he’s experiencing political persecution has no basis. The cases are clear, and they involve not only qualified human trafficking.)
The Palace’s comment came after Department of the Interior and Local Government Secretary Jonvic Remulla said in a separate press briefing earlier Tuesday that Roque’s asylum request had been denied.
Remulla previously said Roque was applying for asylum in Austria, citing political persecution.
In the Philippines, Roque faces non-bailable qualified human trafficking charges filed by the Department of Justice over his alleged active participation in the operations of Lucky South 99, the illegal Philippine offshore gaming operator (POGO) hub in Pampanga, which was raided in 2024.
An arrest warrant was issued by a Pampanga court against Roque and his co-accused in May 2025 for the qualified human trafficking case.
Meanwhile, in March this year, a group of farmers from Bataan filed land-grabbing complaints against Roque for allegedly transferring land titles, which were supposed to be distributed to 100 farmers, to a private corporation connected to a POGO firm.
The corporation's listed address supposedly pointed to Roque’s office.
The Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR) also filed a tax evasion case against Roque and his wife in April this year for allegedly failing to pay P3.35 million in taxes connected to transactions involving Biancham Holdings and Trading Inc.
Roque denied all accusations, saying these are all part of the continuous political attacks against him.
He also dismissed Remulla’s claim that his asylum request had been denied, calling it “fake news.”
Roque, who served as the Palace spokesperson under then-President Rodrigo Duterte, left the Philippines in 2024.

deduped_items.title: DeepSeek AI engineer slams Anthropic, OpenAI over ‘pacing’ calls, invokes Nazi Germany
deduped_items.summary: A DeepSeek engineer has issued a stark warning about the potential concentration of advanced artificial intelligence and resources in proprietary US developers Anthropic and OpenAI, intensifying a growing debate in China over calls by US industry leaders to “pace” AI development amid safety concerns. The comments preceded an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on September 24, where AI safety may emerge as a key point of dialogue as the two countries race.
deduped_items.body_text:
Advertisement
DeepSeek AI engineer slams Anthropic, OpenAI over ‘pacing’ calls, invokes Nazi Germany
Heated rhetoric highlights tensions over how quickly artificial intelligence should advance and who should shape its future amid mounting safety concerns
3-MIN READ3-MIN
A DeepSeek engineer has issued a stark warning about the potential concentration of advanced artificial intelligence and resources in proprietary US developers Anthropic and OpenAI, intensifying a growing debate in China over calls by US industry leaders to “pace” AI development amid safety concerns.
The comments preceded an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on September 24, where AI safety may emerge as a key point of dialogue as the two countries race for technological supremacy.
Liu Shengyu, a DeepSeek engineer behind the company’s V4.1 models, said he did not trust Anthropic or OpenAI to make cutting-edge AI “open and affordable”, contrasting their closed-source approach with DeepSeek’s embrace of open-source models.
“I especially don’t want Anthropic to master the most advanced artificial intelligence or AGI,” he wrote in a social media post on Monday. AGI broadly refers to AI systems that match or surpass human-level intelligence.

deduped_items.summary: Financial and systemic obstacles are preventing South African blood cancer patients from receiving stem cell transplants even after a match is found. deduped_items.body_text:

            Taiwan urged to boost defense spending‘FRONTLINE’ NATIONS: ‘Vilnius and Taipei are not two separate stories ... whichever of us folds first makes taking the other one cheaper,’ a Lithuanian lawmaker said
  - By Hollie Younger / Staff writer, with CNA
 Lithuanian lawmaker Dovile Sakaliene over the weekend urged Taiwan to prioritize its defense budget, saying that national security cannot be compromised for other public policies, during a joint conference of Taiwanese associations in Helsinki. She made the comments at this year’s Joint Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Taiwanese Associations and the European Federation of Taiwanese Associations, which took place from Friday to Sunday. The event, themed “Democratic Resilience and Trusted Democracy,” drew more than 330 participants, including politicians and human rights advocates from Taiwan, Finland, Lithuania, Poland and the UK, to discuss how democratic societies can resist legal, diplomatic and military coercion by authoritarian states. Attendees pose for a photograph in front of a banner reading “Democratic Resilience & Trusted Solidarity” during the joint annual conference of the World Federation of Taiwanese Associations and the European Federation of Taiwanese Associations in Helsinki over the weekend.Photo: CNA “Taiwan and Ukraine are the structural safety pins of global stability. Pull them and the whole transatlantic system unzips,” Sakaliene wrote on social media yesterday. “Vilnius and Taipei are not two separate stories. Russia and China are one problem working two fronts, and whichever of us folds first makes taking the other one cheaper,” she added. Sakaliene served as Lithuania’s minister of national defense from December 2024 to October last year, when she stepped down following disputes over increasing defense spending. She gave a presentation over the weekend titled: “Resilience Under Pressure: Lessons from Lithuania and NATO’s Eastern Flank,” and participated in the panel “Frontline Democracies — Geopolitical Resilience in an Era of Authoritarian Pressure.” Taiwan must invest sufficient resources to maintain its self-defense capabilities, as China’s military aircraft and exercises have become the “new normal,” she said. If you cannot protect your country, then who would be left to benefit from education spending, she asked, adding that if nations do not strengthen their own military, they are only strengthening that of the enemy. As cooperation grows between China, Russia, Iran and North Korea, Taiwan faces a similar situation to Europe, she said. There are no shortcuts to democratic resilience; it is built day by day through strengthening social trust, maintaining defense capabilities and ensuring that democratic institutions can continue functioning during a crisis, said Atte Harjanne, member of the Finnish parliament and First Vice Chair of the Taiwan Friendship Group. Since China enacted the Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress in July, concerns are growing that Beijing’s domestic laws could be applied outside of China, and Taiwan must now be on even higher alert, Overseas Community Affairs Council Minister Hsu Chia-ching (徐佳青) said. Taiwanese officials, civil servants, those involved in religious exchanges and those working in technology with access to sensitive information are now high-risk groups when traveling to China, she said. Luke de Pulford, cofounder and executive director of the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), said that the alliance has faced continued interference from the Chinese government since its establishment, including members being sanctioned or denied visas, having their identities impersonated or being targeted with sexual images generated by artificial intelligence. Before IPAC held its summit in Taipei, Beijing obtained the list of delegates and pressured politicians from 11 countries to prevent them from attending, he said. deduped_items.title: VP praises Taiwan’s visibility, nations’ attention
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            VP praises Taiwan’s visibility, nations’ attentionPLEDGE: Europe and Taiwan would remain steadfast in upholding a free and democratic way of life and maintaining regional peace and prosperity, Hsiao said
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim (蕭美琴) yesterday said that she saw a growing number of international friends willing to learn about Taiwan and hear its story during her visit to the Italian island of Ventotene last week. “Throughout this journey, I have once again felt the international community’s concern for Taiwan, and encountered a growing number of good friends willing to learn about Taiwan and hear its story,” Hsiao said at Taiwan Taoyuan International Airport upon returning from Italy. The most significant part of the trip was “having Taiwan’s voice heard by so many more people in a place of such historical significance,” Hsiao said, referring to the Second Ventotene European Conference for Freedom and Democracy, which she attended last week. Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim, seated, third left, and Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung, seated, fourth left, attend a dinner hosted by European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno on the Italian island of Ventotene on Friday.Photo courtesy of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Hsiao said that Ventotene has an extraordinary history. During World War II, the island was used to detain political dissidents, including Altiero Spinelli, who coauthored a text there that later became known as the Ventotene Manifesto, advocating a federal Europe after the war. Hsiao cited remarks from her Friday address at the Italian conference, saying: “Whether it is Ventotene or Taiwan, no island is too small to have a voice, and no island or society is too small to deserve respect.” Although Europe today is vastly different from the Europe of World War II, democracies around the world continue to face similar challenges, she said. “Authoritarianism, ‘gray zone’ threats, and challenges involving coercion and attempts to alter the ‘status quo’ continue to arise in various forms and locations — challenges with which Taiwan is all too familiar,” she said. Hsiao said that is why she told at the conference that Taiwan, like its European friends, would remain steadfast in upholding a free and democratic way of life, and committed to maintaining regional peace and prosperity. The trip was not announced in advance to avoid “unnecessary interference,” she said, referring to China’s objections. Hsiao was invited by European Parliament Vice President Pina Picierno, the main initiator of the conference, and Carlo Corazza, head of the European Parliament Liaison Office in Italy, to speak at the meeting, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a news release yesterday. Aside from meeting Picierno and Corazza, Hsiao and Minister of Foreign Affairs Lin Chia-lung (林佳龍) also met with Sandro Gozi, chair of the European Parliament’s Delegation to the EU-UK Parliamentary Partnership Assembly; European Parliament member Valerie Hayer; and Ventotene Mayor Carmine Caputo while on the Italian island. Before returning to Taiwan, Hsiao and Lin toured the renowned Roman cisterns and the Museo Storico Archeologico, which houses archeological discoveries from the island, the ministry said.

deduped_items.title: SkyGuardian drones bought from US tested, source says
deduped_items.body_text:
- 
            SkyGuardian drones bought from US tested, source says
  - Staff writer, with CNA
 The first two of the four MQ-9B “SkyGuardian” drones Taiwan purchased from the US underwent their first flight tests at an air base in eastern Taiwan early yesterday, a source familiar with the matter said. The unnamed source did not disclose further details about the test flights, saying that they were conducted at Hualien Air Base. The tests were conducted after the military and the drone manufacturer completed the assembly of the two drones delivered to Taiwan earlier this year, the source added. An MQ-9B drone taxis at Hualien Air Base yesterday. A retired F-5E jet serving as a decoy aircraft is visible in the background.Photo: Yu Tai-lang, Taipei Times On March 17, Deputy Minister of National Defense Hsu Szu-chien (徐斯儉) and Representative to the US Alexander Yui (俞大?) attended a handover ceremony in the US for two of the MQ-9Bs. The US has agreed to deliver the four MQ-9Bs to Taiwan in two batches this year and next year. The MQ-9Bs would provide Taiwan with “intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance, target acquisition, and counter-land, counter-sea and anti-submarine strike capabilities,” according to the US Defense Security Cooperation Agency. Su Tzu-yun (蘇紫雲), a research fellow at the government-funded Institute for National Defense and Security Research (INDSR), previously said that the role of the MQ-9Bs in Taiwan is to enhance battlefield reconnaissance and surveillance capabilities rather than serve as a primary offensive weapon. INDSR researcher Hsieh Pei-shiue (謝沛學) wrote in 2020, when the US first approved the sale to Taiwan, that the drone is capable of linking to satellite communications networks shared among US allies. That means Taiwan and the US could share battlefield intelligence instantly, providing opportunities for the two sides to cooperate during a conflict. For example, if a cross-strait conflict breaks out, Washington could take advantage of anti-ship missile systems deployed along the First Island Chain to prevent Chinese People’s Liberation Army vessels from sailing into waters east of Taiwan to blockade the nation, Hsieh said. MQ-9Bs are capable of long-term, long-range surveillance, meaning the drones could fly near Chinese vessels and provide critical intelligence for US forces to target them, Hsieh wrote at the time. Another INDSR researcher, Kao Chih-jung (高志榮), yesterday cautioned that while the MQ-9B can detect and classify a large number of targets at once, it still requires final visual identification by human operators. That limits the drone to conducting detailed, continuous surveillance on only two or three targets simultaneously, Kao said. Consequently, the military should not rely solely on a handful of large drones, but should instead utilize the MQ-9B to conduct wide-area scans and designate high-value targets, he said. That intelligence could then be distributed to small and medium-sized drones, shore-based radars and other combat units to build a more resilient “integrated reconnaissance and strike” network, he added. Additional reporting by Aaron Tu

deduped_items.title: DeepSeek AI engineer slams Anthropic, OpenAI over ‘pacing’ calls, invokes Nazi Germany
deduped_items.summary: A DeepSeek engineer has issued a stark warning about the potential concentration of advanced artificial intelligence and resources in proprietary US developers Anthropic and OpenAI, intensifying a growing debate in China over calls by US industry leaders to “pace” AI development amid safety concerns. The comments preceded an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on September 24, where AI safety may emerge as a key point of dialogue as the two countries race.
deduped_items.body_text:
Advertisement
DeepSeek AI engineer slams Anthropic, OpenAI over ‘pacing’ calls, invokes Nazi Germany
Heated rhetoric highlights tensions over how quickly artificial intelligence should advance and who should shape its future amid mounting safety concerns
3-MIN READ3-MIN
A DeepSeek engineer has issued a stark warning about the potential concentration of advanced artificial intelligence and resources in proprietary US developers Anthropic and OpenAI, intensifying a growing debate in China over calls by US industry leaders to “pace” AI development amid safety concerns.
The comments preceded an expected meeting between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump on September 24, where AI safety may emerge as a key point of dialogue as the two countries race for technological supremacy.
Liu Shengyu, a DeepSeek engineer behind the company’s V4.1 models, said he did not trust Anthropic or OpenAI to make cutting-edge AI “open and affordable”, contrasting their closed-source approach with DeepSeek’s embrace of open-source models.
“I especially don’t want Anthropic to master the most advanced artificial intelligence or AGI,” he wrote in a social media post on Monday. AGI broadly refers to AI systems that match or surpass human-level intelligence.

deduped_items.summary: Study finds earlier numbers were underestimated, suggesting impact of diseases and massacres were much greater than previously thoughtGet our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcastThe number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Australia before colonisation was dramatically underestimated, according to new research that suggests many more of them were killed.Modelling by a national research group puts the population levels before the 1788 first fleet arrived at 2.2 mil
deduped_items.body_text:
The number of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in Australia before colonisation was dramatically underestimated, according to new research that suggests many more of them were killed.
Modelling by a national research group puts the population levels before the 1788 first fleet arrived at 2.2 million, compared with early estimates of 250,000 people.
The research, by the Australian Research Council Centre of Excellence for Indigenous and Environmental Histories and Futures (CIEHF), has been published in the peer-reviewed Nature Human Behaviour.
The authors wrote that, historically, population estimates have been poor “due to lethal diseases, frontier and structural violence, and absence of systematic censuses” and that it’s “invaluable to truth-telling and reconciliation” to try to rectify that.
They warn readers that the content of the study is confronting and possibly distressing.
The modelling showed there had to be millions of excess deaths from smallpox and other diseases, massacres, and the other results of colonisation such as dispossession and malnutrition, according to co-author Prof Corey Bradshaw, a global ecology professor at Flinders University.
His previous research found that an 1789 smallpox outbreak alone killed as many as 220,000 Aboriginal people. There were also other smallpox epidemics, as well as outbreaks of measles, influenza, tuberculosis, typhoid and other diseases.
Bradshaw said he would bet his career that massacre databases were underestimated by an “order of magnitude”.
“If you’re a frontier farmer, a colonialist that came out to a new area, and you were trying to remove people from ‘your’ land, you’re not going to write extensively about how many people you killed to do that,” he said.
“There’s another component here that’s essentially greed and racism – the entire concept of terra nullius was based on not many people being here. If there’s a systematic desire to take land [fewer people means a] better justification for imperialism.”
Australia was colonised on the basis of terra nullius, that it belonged to no one. That concept was overthrown with the high court’s Mabo decision, when it was recognised that First Nations people had been here for tens of thousands of years.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people were not properly counted in the census until 1971, after the 1967 referendum. At that point, 115,953 people identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander.
In 2021, 812,728 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people were counted in the census, a figure revised upwards to 983,257 with post-census recounts.
The estimate of 2.2 million, as well as a new estimate of 2.06 million excess deaths between 1788 and 1861, means the population was reduced to about 7% of its original size.
“We are not talking about a marginal consequence of colonisation but a demographic catastrophe at the heart of the Australian story,” distinguished professor Larissa Behrendt said. A Euahleyai/Gamillaroi woman, she is also the chair of the CIEHF’s advisory committee.
Early on after colonisation, various people estimated how many Aboriginal people were in their region. For example, governor Arthur Phillip estimated Gadigal people of the Eora nation came to about 1,500.
The first continent-wide estimate by social anthropologist Alfred Radcliffe-Brown put the number between 250,000 and 300,000, but mainly used observations from after the impacts of colonisation had been felt.
Radcliffe-Brown was aware that it was an underestimate, but many researchers since have relied on that count as a baseline. Again, they often recognised it would be an undercount because of historical reasons and changes in who identified or was identified as Aboriginal.
In 1983, economic historian Noel Butlin estimated the population at about 900,000. Later he increased that to between 1.1 million and 1.3 million. In 1987, archaeologists John Mulvaney and J Peter White argued it was more likely 750,000.

“If you’re a frontier farmer, a colonialist that came out to a new area, and you were trying to remove people from ‘your’ land, you’re not going to write extensively about how many people you killed to do that,” he said.
“There’s another component here that’s essentially greed and racism – the entire concept of terra nullius was based on not many people being here. If there’s a systematic desire to take land [fewer people means a] better justification for imperialism.”
Australia was colonised on the basis of terra nullius, that it belonged to no one. That concept was overthrown with the high court’s Mabo decision, when it was recognised that First Nations people had been here for tens of thousands of years.
Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people were not properly counted in the census until 1971, after the 1967 referendum. At that point, 115,953 people identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander.
In 2021, 812,728 Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people were counted in the census, a figure revised upwards to 983,257 with post-census recounts.
The estimate of 2.2 million, as well as a new estimate of 2.06 million excess deaths between 1788 and 1861, means the population was reduced to about 7% of its original size.
“We are not talking about a marginal consequence of colonisation but a demographic catastrophe at the heart of the Australian story,” distinguished professor Larissa Behrendt said. A Euahleyai/Gamillaroi woman, she is also the chair of the CIEHF’s advisory committee.
Early on after colonisation, various people estimated how many Aboriginal people were in their region. For example, governor Arthur Phillip estimated Gadigal people of the Eora nation came to about 1,500.
The first continent-wide estimate by social anthropologist Alfred Radcliffe-Brown put the number between 250,000 and 300,000, but mainly used observations from after the impacts of colonisation had been felt.
Radcliffe-Brown was aware that it was an underestimate, but many researchers since have relied on that count as a baseline. Again, they often recognised it would be an undercount because of historical reasons and changes in who identified or was identified as Aboriginal.
In 1983, economic historian Noel Butlin estimated the population at about 900,000. Later he increased that to between 1.1 million and 1.3 million. In 1987, archaeologists John Mulvaney and J Peter White argued it was more likely 750,000.

deduped_items.title: Clément Hervieu-Léger, l’avenir de la Comédie-Française
deduped_items.summary: L’administrateur général parle du rôle que le Québec pourrait tenir dans l’avenir de la prestigieuse compagnie qu’il dirige.
deduped_items.body_text:
Clément Hervieu-Léger a été nommé administrateur général de la Comédie-Française le 4 août 2025. De passage à Montréal à l’occasion de la tournée québécoise et canadienne de Lumières, lumières, lumières, la pièce d’Evelyne de la Chenelière mise en scène par Florent Siaud avec deux actrices de la Maison de Molière, Florence Viala et Aymeline Alix, le comédien, metteur en scène et pédagogue, à la tête d’une troupe permanente de 57 comédiens et comédiennes, a pris le temps de nous parler de tradition, mais aussi d’innovation et du rôle que le Québec pourrait occuper dans ses plans d’avenir.
Cette première coproduction avec une compagnie québécoise, Les songes turbulents, que dirige Florent Siaud, Clément Hervieu-Léger la considère comme une manière pour la Comédie-Française, qui existe depuis 1680, ce qui en fait la troupe en activité la plus ancienne au monde, d’« aller vers le public ». « Comme institution, je trouve que c’est essentiel de ne pas seulement attendre que le public vienne à nous. C’était donc nécessaire, pour moi, d’être ici. Je n’aurais pas imaginé que ce spectacle soit ici, que la Comédie-Française soit à Montréal et au Québec, sans que l’administrateur général soit présent. »
Clément Hervieu-Léger, qui était de la distribution de Lucrèce Borgia, un spectacle que la Comédie-Française a présenté au théâtre du Nouveau Monde à l’été 2017, à l’occasion des festivités du 375e anniversaire de Montréal, tenait à revenir dans la métropole et à rencontrer des artistes et des artisans d’ici. « Le Québec, c’est et ce doit être un interlocuteur privilégié pour la Comédie-Française. C’est pourquoi ça m’importait de venir à la rencontre des gens, des directeurs, des directrices, mais aussi d’aller voir des lieux, d’avoir une vision un peu plus précise de la cartographie théâtrale québécoise. Je suis très ouvert à l’idée d’imaginer de nouvelles formes de collaboration. Il y a plein de choses qui sont possibles, que ce soient des coproductions, des accueils ou que sais-je encore. La création de Lumières, lumières, lumières en est la preuve. »
Plans d’avenir
Le mandat de Clément Hervieu-Léger est de cinq ans. Sa première année en poste n’a pas été de tout repos, notamment à cause de travaux importants réalisés dans la salle Richelieu, celle que la troupe occupe depuis 1799, la plus grande des trois salles dont dispose la Comédie-Française. « Les travaux sont terminés, annonce fièrement l’administrateur général. Toutes les équipes sont revenues, et les spectacles vont reprendre à partir du 15 octobre. »
                                                    « Comme institution, je trouve que c’est essentiel de ne pas seulement attendre que le public vienne à nous. C’était donc nécessaire, pour moi, d’être ici [au Québec]. »
Clément Hervieu-Léger
Photo: Marie-France Coallier Le Devoir
L’un des chevaux de bataille de l’homme, c’est le rapport au répertoire. « On se doit de l’interroger, explique-t-il. Il faut s’interdire de le concevoir comme une bibliothèque un peu muséale de textes anciens qu’on continuerait à jouer sans trop savoir pourquoi. Est-ce que les pièces qui nous arrivent du XVIIe et du XVIIIe siècles, qu’on a beaucoup jouées, continuent à être pertinentes pour éclairer le monde contemporain ? Le répertoire, c’est un bien commun qui doit s’enrichir, qui doit être malaxé. »
Clément Hervieu-Léger tient à ce que la maison qu’il dirige « demeure en phase avec le monde qui l’entoure ». « Le théâtre, c’est l’occasion de faire l’expérience de notre commune humanité, mais aussi celle de trouver des clés pour appréhender un monde qui est sacrément complexe et parfois très angoissant. » Pour l’administrateur, être de son temps, ça passe notamment par l’espace accordé aux femmes. « On n’a pas toujours, à la Comédie-Française, donné aux autrices la place qui leur revient. Elles ont été très invisibilisées pendant des siècles. Il y a là, selon moi, quelque chose à réparer. »
Il se réjouit de dire que, cette saison, au Vieux-Colombier,

deduped_items.summary: L’administrateur général parle du rôle que le Québec pourrait tenir dans l’avenir de la prestigieuse compagnie qu’il dirige.

Cette première coproduction avec une compagnie québécoise, Les songes turbulents, que dirige Florent Siaud, Clément Hervieu-Léger la considère comme une manière pour la Comédie-Française, qui existe depuis 1680, ce qui en fait la troupe en activité la plus ancienne au monde, d’« aller vers le public ». « Comme institution, je trouve que c’est essentiel de ne pas seulement attendre que le public vienne à nous. deduped_items.title: Javier Aranda Luna: El gimnasio bíblico de Monsiváis
deduped_items.summary: Hay una paradoja magnética en la biografía intelectual de Carlos Monsiváis. El cronista insomne de la Ciudad de México, el crítico feroz del poder político, el gozoso y falso ateo que diseccionaba la iconosfera y la cultura popular, aprendió a leer –y a debatir– en el seno de una cultura protestante. Antes de ser el gran exégeta de la urbe, el jubiloso hermeneuta del cine, el minucioso cirujano que diseccionó las entretelas de la clase política, fue un niño que empuñaba la Biblia como una espada

deduped_items.title: Zohran Mamdani contra Trump: Nueva York y otros 21 estados demandan al gobierno de EE.UU. por la norma de "carga pública" y dificultar que algunos inmigrantes obtengan la tarjeta de residencia permanente
deduped_items.summary: A días de que entre en vigor la nueva versión de la norma de "carga pública", el alcalde neoyorquino Zohran Mamdani y la fiscal general Letitia James encabezan una doble ofensiva legal junto a 22 estados y las principales metrópolis del país.Las demandas buscan bloquear una medida que permitiría denegar la tarjeta de residencia a inmigrantes legales por usar ayudas como Medicaid o cupones de alimentos, poniendo en juego más de 2.200 millones de dólares en fondos federales para los estados demand
deduped_items.body_text:
El alcalde de la ciudad de Nueva York, Zohran Mamdani, y la fiscal general del estado, Letitia James, encabezan una masiva ofensiva judicial contra la administración de Donald Trump para frenar la entrada en vigor de la nueva norma sobre "carga pública". La acción legal, presentada ante el Tribunal Federal de Manhattan por una coalición de 22 estados y media docena de las ciudades más pobladas de Estados Unidos, busca impedir que el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) aplique a partir de este viernes criterios drásticamente más severos para denegar la residencia permanente y las visas a inmigrantes con estatus legal.
— Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani (@NYCMayor) September 14, 2026
La controversia gira en torno a la ampliación discrecional de los beneficios públicos no monetarios que los agentes de inmigración podrán considerar como un factor negativo. Bajo el nuevo marco, la solicitud o uso de asistencia médica a través de Medicaid, el subsidio de alimentos SNAP e incluso la participación en programas de almuerzos escolares gratuitos podrán ser utilizados para calificar a un solicitante como dependiente del Estado, afectando incluso a familias de estatus mixto con hijos que son ciudadanos estadounidenses por nacimiento.
El impacto en la salud pública y el temor en las comunidades
Durante la presentación del recurso judicial en el Ayuntamiento de Manhattan, Mamdani advirtió sobre las consecuencias letales que provocará el retraimiento de las familias ante el temor de poner en riesgo sus trámites migratorios. El alcalde citó análisis del Departamento de Salud municipal que prevén un incremento del 10,6% en la tasa de mortalidad prematura en vecindarios inmigrantes durante los próximos cinco años, producto de la interrupción en la atención médica y la nutrición básica.
La preocupación central de los demandantes radica en el "efecto disuasorio" que ya se registra en metrópolis como Nueva York, Chicago, San Francisco y Seattle. Cálculos incluidos en las demandas estiman que cerca de 4 millones de personas a nivel nacional podrían darse de baja voluntariamente de la red de protección social para evitar represalias administrativas, una cifra que incluye a 1,8 millones de niños que perderían la cobertura médica o la asistencia alimentaria a la que tienen derecho por ley.
Un choque multimillonario por la autoridad federal
Más allá del impacto social, la batalla legal abarca un severo perjuicio financiero para las arcas estatales y locales. De acuerdo con los documentos presentados en el Distrito Sur de Nueva York, los estados calculan una pérdida directa de 4.050 millones de dólares anuales en transferencias federales para programas de salud, de los cuales 2.200 millones corresponden exclusivamente a las 22 entidades demandantes. Las autoridades locales sostienen que la falta de atención preventiva obligará a los hospitales públicos y redes de emergencia a asumir costos operativos de crisis mucho más elevados.
La estrategia legal del bloque opositor argumenta que el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional incurrió en un exceso de atribuciones al interpretar la figura de la "carga pública", sobrepasando los límites históricos fijados por el Congreso desde 1882. Ante las acusaciones de arbitrariedad, el gobierno federal defendió la medida argumentando la necesidad de restablecer la autosuficiencia de los solicitantes, mientras el tribunal analiza si emite una orden de restricción temporal antes de que las nuevas reglas comiencen a aplicarse formalmente.
Qué es la regla de "carga pública" y cuál es su origen
La disposición de la "carga pública" es un precepto de la ley de inmigración de Estados Unidos que data de 1882, creado originalmente para evitar que el Estado asumiera la manutención total de personas incapaces de autosustentarse. Durante más de un siglo, las autoridades de inmigración aplicaron este principio evaluando casi de forma exclusiva la recepción de asistencia económica directa en efectivo, como subsidios por invalidez o ingreso

La acción legal, presentada ante el Tribunal Federal de Manhattan por una coalición de 22 estados y media docena de las ciudades más pobladas de Estados Unidos, busca impedir que el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional (DHS) aplique a partir de este viernes criterios drásticamente más severos para denegar la residencia permanente y las visas a inmigrantes con estatus legal.
— Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani (@NYCMayor) September 14, 2026
La controversia gira en torno a la ampliación discrecional de los beneficios públicos no monetarios que los agentes de inmigración podrán considerar como un factor negativo. Bajo el nuevo marco, la solicitud o uso de asistencia médica a través de Medicaid, el subsidio de alimentos SNAP e incluso la participación en programas de almuerzos escolares gratuitos podrán ser utilizados para calificar a un solicitante como dependiente del Estado, afectando incluso a familias de estatus mixto con hijos que son ciudadanos estadounidenses por nacimiento.
El impacto en la salud pública y el temor en las comunidades
Durante la presentación del recurso judicial en el Ayuntamiento de Manhattan, Mamdani advirtió sobre las consecuencias letales que provocará el retraimiento de las familias ante el temor de poner en riesgo sus trámites migratorios. El alcalde citó análisis del Departamento de Salud municipal que prevén un incremento del 10,6% en la tasa de mortalidad prematura en vecindarios inmigrantes durante los próximos cinco años, producto de la interrupción en la atención médica y la nutrición básica.
La preocupación central de los demandantes radica en el "efecto disuasorio" que ya se registra en metrópolis como Nueva York, Chicago, San Francisco y Seattle. Cálculos incluidos en las demandas estiman que cerca de 4 millones de personas a nivel nacional podrían darse de baja voluntariamente de la red de protección social para evitar represalias administrativas, una cifra que incluye a 1,8 millones de niños que perderían la cobertura médica o la asistencia alimentaria a la que tienen derecho por ley.
Un choque multimillonario por la autoridad federal
Más allá del impacto social, la batalla legal abarca un severo perjuicio financiero para las arcas estatales y locales. De acuerdo con los documentos presentados en el Distrito Sur de Nueva York, los estados calculan una pérdida directa de 4.050 millones de dólares anuales en transferencias federales para programas de salud, de los cuales 2.200 millones corresponden exclusivamente a las 22 entidades demandantes. Las autoridades locales sostienen que la falta de atención preventiva obligará a los hospitales públicos y redes de emergencia a asumir costos operativos de crisis mucho más elevados.
La estrategia legal del bloque opositor argumenta que el Departamento de Seguridad Nacional incurrió en un exceso de atribuciones al interpretar la figura de la "carga pública", sobrepasando los límites históricos fijados por el Congreso desde 1882. Ante las acusaciones de arbitrariedad, el gobierno federal defendió la medida argumentando la necesidad de restablecer la autosuficiencia de los solicitantes, mientras el tribunal analiza si emite una orden de restricción temporal antes de que las nuevas reglas comiencen a aplicarse formalmente.
Qué es la regla de "carga pública" y cuál es su origen
La disposición de la "carga pública" es un precepto de la ley de inmigración de Estados Unidos que data de 1882, creado originalmente para evitar que el Estado asumiera la manutención total de personas incapaces de autosustentarse. Durante más de un siglo, las autoridades de inmigración aplicaron este principio evaluando casi de forma exclusiva la recepción de asistencia económica directa en efectivo, como subsidios por invalidez o ingreso

deduped_items.summary: A días de que entre en vigor la nueva versión de la norma de "carga pública", el alcalde neoyorquino Zohran Mamdani y la fiscal general Letitia James encabezan una doble ofensiva legal junto a 22 estados y las principales metrópolis del país.Las demandas buscan bloquear una medida que permitiría denegar la tarjeta de residencia a inmigrantes legales por usar ayudas como Medicaid o cupones de alimentos, poniendo en juego más de 2.200 millones de dólares en fondos federales para los estados demand

¿Qué hay detrás de los temores de que la IA extinguirá a la humanidad para el 2030? Las claves de las advertencias de la ONU
Acelerado uso en las guerras y servicios financieros, entre las alertas. EE. UU. insiste en la desregulación, mientras que China, en su uso 'abierto'.
El vertiginoso ascenso de los modelos de lenguaje y la etiqueta de inteligencia artificial en nuevos productos —desde celulares y computadores hasta lavadoras y neveras— ha causado un aumento casi proporcional en los temores de que la inteligencia artificial (IA) reemplace o incluso acabe con los humanos.
Sin embargo, en los últimos días, especialmente tras las advertencias del investigador de Anthropic Jacob Coxon —quien señaló que esta tecnología extinguiría a la humanidad para 2030—, estas preocupaciones alcanzaron un nuevo nivel y se cruzaron con la disputa abierta entre Estados Unidos y China por el liderazgo de esta tecnología.
"Todos los derechos humanos están en riesgo, incluidos los derechos a la vida, la alimentación, la privacidad, la salud y la seguridad", debido al acelerado desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, advirtió este lunes el alto comisionado de la ONU, Volker Türk, quien instó a los Estados y a las empresas "a movilizarse urgentemente en el marco de instancias multilaterales".
Türk, quien considera que "estamos al borde de un cambio irreversible, que nos afecta no solo a nosotros, sino a las generaciones futuras de la humanidad", advirtió que los sistemas más avanzados de la IA representan un riesgo sin precedentes.
"La actual carrera hacia una IA cada vez más potente supone un salto cualitativo hacia mayores riesgos existenciales para todos los aspectos de nuestras vidas", agregó el jefe de derechos humanos de la ONU, después de que empleados de ese sector tecnológico urgieron a ralentizar el avance de esa tecnología.
I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.

¿Qué hay detrás de los temores de que la IA extinguirá a la humanidad para el 2030? Las claves de las advertencias de la ONU
Acelerado uso en las guerras y servicios financieros, entre las alertas. EE. UU. insiste en la desregulación, mientras que China, en su uso 'abierto'.
El vertiginoso ascenso de los modelos de lenguaje y la etiqueta de inteligencia artificial en nuevos productos —desde celulares y computadores hasta lavadoras y neveras— ha causado un aumento casi proporcional en los temores de que la inteligencia artificial (IA) reemplace o incluso acabe con los humanos.
Sin embargo, en los últimos días, especialmente tras las advertencias del investigador de Anthropic Jacob Coxon —quien señaló que esta tecnología extinguiría a la humanidad para 2030—, estas preocupaciones alcanzaron un nuevo nivel y se cruzaron con la disputa abierta entre Estados Unidos y China por el liderazgo de esta tecnología.
"Todos los derechos humanos están en riesgo, incluidos los derechos a la vida, la alimentación, la privacidad, la salud y la seguridad", debido al acelerado desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, advirtió este lunes el alto comisionado de la ONU, Volker Türk, quien instó a los Estados y a las empresas "a movilizarse urgentemente en el marco de instancias multilaterales".
Türk, quien considera que "estamos al borde de un cambio irreversible, que nos afecta no solo a nosotros, sino a las generaciones futuras de la humanidad", advirtió que los sistemas más avanzados de la IA representan un riesgo sin precedentes.
"La actual carrera hacia una IA cada vez más potente supone un salto cualitativo hacia mayores riesgos existenciales para todos los aspectos de nuestras vidas", agregó el jefe de derechos humanos de la ONU, después de que empleados de ese sector tecnológico urgieron a ralentizar el avance de esa tecnología.
I resigned from Anthropic today. I spent the last three years doing pretraining research at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Neither company is acting responsibly. They are racing straight to self-improving superintelligence and gambling with our lives. More thoughts below.

Türk, quien considera que "estamos al borde de un cambio irreversible, que nos afecta no solo a nosotros, sino a las generaciones futuras de la humanidad", advirtió que los sistemas más avanzados de la IA representan un riesgo sin precedentes.
"La actual carrera hacia una IA cada vez más potente supone un salto cualitativo hacia mayores riesgos existenciales para todos los aspectos de nuestras vidas", agregó el jefe de derechos humanos de la ONU, después de que empleados de ese sector tecnológico urgieron a ralentizar el avance de esa tecnología.

deduped_items.summary: An investigation by ARI and Convoca found a slight shift in who controls the Mining Arc following the apparent killing of the TDA leader
deduped_items.body_text:
After US Intervention, Crime Still Controls Venezuelan Mines (Part I)
An investigation by ARI and Convoca found a slight shift in who controls the Mining Arc following the apparent killing of the TDA leader
This is an abridged version of the original story in Spanish, the second part of award-winning investigative journalism project Dorada Opacidad. We will publish the second (and last) part of this investigation tomorrow.
When they pass through the streets of the Las Claritas–Kilómetro 88 mining corridor in Bolívar state, southern Venezuela, a thick, yellowish cloud of dust blankets them like a veil. The sound is unmistakable: a convoy of 15, 20, or 25 motorcycles riding together. Aboard are soldiers from the Orinoco Mining Arc Protection Group (GPAMO)—a unit conceived and activated in 2022 under the command of the Strategic Operational Command of the Bolivarian National Armed Forces (CEOFANB) to safeguard the deposits. They had never been there before June 9, 2026, when three rockets, shot by a US aircraft, shook the area’s flimsy houses. Now, GPAMO is the law.
Although some cover their faces, Rafael knows them well. He owns one of the gold mills operating at the El Mecatico mine—one of many in an area that holds the world’s fourth-largest gold deposit, according to a 2018 certification by Canadian mining company Gold Reserve. Standing beneath the tin roof that shelters his business, he explained that he would soon have to pay the GPAMO 20 grams of gold (roughly 2,000 US dollars) in exchange for a registration form that in theory is free. He is also required to make monthly payments to remain on the site.
For Rafael and the residents of Las Claritas, everything changed on the morning of June 9, when they woke up to find the area occupied by the military. In the early hours, dozens of vehicles transported hundreds of troops from various branches of the Bolivarian National Armed Forces (FANB)—such as the Special Affairs Directorate (DAE) of the General Directorate of Military Counterintelligence (DGCIM)—who patrolled the streets alongside unidentified men dressed in black and carrying long guns. Meanwhile, a pair of military aviation Cougar helicopters flew just above the rooftops of the houses.
The objective of that mobilization was to dismantle “The System.” That was the name given to the criminal alliance between Juan Gabriel Rivas Núñez—known as “Negro Juancho”—and Yohan José Romero (nicknamed “Johan Petrica” or “El Viejo”), one of the leaders of the “mega-gang” born in the Tocorón prison: the Tren de Aragua. For over a decade, this criminal alliance had dominated the territory containing one of the world’s largest gold mining complexes—Las Brisas-Las Cristinas—and had subjugated the local population through torture, mutilation, and murder.
All signs pointed to a “change of government”—a term used in the Venezuelan criminal underworld to describe one criminal group replacing another in a territory.
The residents were so terrified that they remained locked in their homes for days. Rafael did not hear the explosions that rang out mid-morning in Brisas de Cuyuní, near the Kilómetro 88 mining area, because he had gone to his ore mill in the early hours of the morning without noticing the military deployment. Hours later, the military arrived in El Mecatico to destroy the warehouses and properties belonging to The System. This operation was repeated at other mines, as well as at hotels, homes, and businesses in the town.
To determine who truly holds power along the Las Claritas-Kilómetro 88 corridor and in the southern mining towns extending as far as Guasipati, a team of reporters from the Alianza Rebelde Investiga (ARI) and Convoca toured the region as part of the investigative series Dorada Opacidad (Golden Opacity). Interviews with more than twenty sources—ranging from merchants, mill operators, police officers, and local residents to religious figures and local government officials—made it possible to map out the new crimi

deduped_items.body_text:
ISLAMABAD: An inquiry committee formed to probe the deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) has found “systemic and institutional failure” and determined that an electrical failure was the most likely cause of the blaze, it emerged on Tuesday.
The August 26 fire at a nursery in Pims’ Mother and Child Hospital claimed the lives of 14 newborns. The incident raised concerns over fire safety measures and sparked calls for accountability, with criminal action being ordered against eight officials.
Headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, the committee was formed on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif’s directives on the day the fire occurred. It has presented its findings and recommendations in a 43-page report available with Dawn.
The committee concluded that “systemic and institutional failure is established, while individual responsibility varies with the strength of the evidence”.
It noted that Pims and its “senior management bear the principal institutional responsibility for failing to convert known risks, prior warnings and assigned duties into an effective safety system”.
“The electrical spark explains how the fire began; the institutional system explains why it became a catastrophe.
“Fourteen newborns were lost not because one safeguard failed, but because too many safeguards were absent, weak, delayed or never verified to be working,” the report declared.
It explained: “The causal chain is coherent. A localised electrical failure most probably started the fire; combustible and oxygen-supported conditions accelerated it; inadequate detection and protection failed to contain it; overcrowding, limited evacuation capacity and the absence of a rehearsed neonatal emergency system constrained rescue; delayed institutional activation weakened response; and longstanding governance, maintenance and regulatory failures allowed these vulnerabilities to coexist.”
The report also pointed out a “history of known but incompletely closed risks”.
It said that earlier correspondence by the Capital Development Authority (CDA), the Federal Ombudsman’s 2015 findings, Pims’ own 2025 acknowledgement of ageing fire safety infrastructure, and especially the July 6, 2026 Nursing Hostel fire had already highlighted deficiencies in detection, alarms, electrical inspection, evacuation, firefighting equipment, drills and emergency planning.
“Yet those warnings had not been converted into a comprehensive, time-bound and independently verified corrective programme before the Nursery fire,” the report regretted.
“The specific AC 2 defect may not have been foreseeable; the need for stronger fire preparedness plainly was.”
The committee said its conclusions were based on a structured 52-task investigation drawing upon forensic evidence, CCTV, call records, engineering and maintenance documents, clinical and casualty records, duty and attendance material, witness statements, contracts, regulatory records, and earlier inquiries.
Response
Citing CCTV footage, which established “an exceptionally rapid emergency”, the report said the evidence “rejects any generalised allegation that frontline personnel abandoned the newborns”.
Noting that Charge Nurse Nasreen Akhtar, Security Guard Maria Saleem and Staff Nurse Razia Noreen responded within moments, the report said that “several acted promptly and courageously in circumstances that became untenable within minutes”.
The report also highlighted the “vulnerability” of the nursery, with 15 “medically fragile, non-self-evacuating neonates were housed in a 10-bed unit, several dependent on oxygen or respiratory support”.w
Only two doctors and two nurses were immediately available, and protected evacuation resources were limited.

deduped_items.title: Africa: New 'Blockbuster' Tuberculosis Vaccines Could Save Seven Million Lives by 2050
deduped_items.summary: [GAVI, the Vaccine Alliance] Next-generation TB vaccines, expected to become available from 2029, could deliver major health and economic gains, helping to save an estimated 7.3 million lives, generate up to US$ 135 billion in economic benefits for low-and middle-income countries by 2050, and support efforts to combat antimicrobial resistance. Action must be taken now to ensure that countries with the highest disease burden are able to access vaccines in sufficient quantities Gavi CEO, Dr Sania

deduped_items.title: Disparition du journaliste Moussa Kaka au Niger: «Le Sahel ne doit pas devenir un trou noir de l'information»
deduped_items.summary: Au Niger, deux semaines après sa disparition, on est toujours sans nouvelles de notre confrère Moussa Kaka. Mais aujourd'hui, Reporters sans frontières (RSF) parle de « disparition forcée » et dit avoir de bonnes raisons de penser que les autorités militaires de Niamey y sont pour quelque chose. Où en est la liberté de la presse au Niger et dans les deux autres pays du Sahel central, le Mali et le Burkina Faso ? Sadibou Marong est le directeur du bureau de RSF pour l'Afrique subsaharienne. deduped_items.title: Au Cameroun, une succession de condamnations coûte plus de 400 milliards de FCFA à l'État
deduped_items.summary: Au Cameroun, des leaders politiques et de la société civile s'alarment d'une série de condamnations contre l'État, dans diverses procédures contentieuses, devant des juridictions internationales. Des condamnations très lourdes sur le plan des indemnisations financières. La presse locale a fait les comptes et fait état de 446 milliards de FCFA, en trois mois (près de 700 millions d'euros), à verser à trois créanciers étrangers avec lesquels l'État du Cameroun avait signé des contrats commerciaux.

Mais aujourd'hui, Reporters sans frontières (RSF) parle de « disparition forcée » et dit avoir de bonnes raisons de penser que les autorités militaires de Niamey y sont pour quelque chose. Où en est la liberté de la presse au Niger et dans les deux autres pays du Sahel central, le Mali et le Burkina Faso ? Sadibou Marong est le directeur du bureau de RSF pour l'Afrique subsaharienne. deduped_items.title: The Atlantic’s October Cover: Anne Applebaum on the “Empire of Grift” and the Revolution in American Foreign Policy
deduped_items.summary: In The Atlantic’s October cover story, “Empire of Grift,” staff writer Anne Applebaum examines how far-right ideologues have transformed American foreign policy into a tool of private gain and antidemocratic reaction. Instead of making the world safe for democracy, she writes, U.S. foreign policy is rewiring the international order. Reporting from Brazil, Applebaum reveals that the United States is not the ally Brazilians once knew. No longer is American power deployed solely by trained diplomat
