deduped_items.summary: Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Tue, 09/15/2026 - 12:35 New England Patriots owner rallied other stadium owners against rapper after he condemned Israel’s genocide of Palestinians Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots, on the field during practice prior to Super Bowl LX at Stanford Stadium on 4 February 2026 in Stanford, California Off In a statement shared on Instagram, US rapper Macklemore confirmed
deduped_items.body_text:
Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour
In a statement shared on Instagram, US rapper Macklemore confirmed that “Ed Sheeran and his team” had dropped him from the tour after he said “Free Palestine”.
The campaign to remove Macklemore from the tour was driven by billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, who threatened to block Sheeran and his team from using his stadium.
Kraft also rallied other stadium owners across the country to stop the tour from proceeding.
“Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium,” Macklemore wrote.
“Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: 'If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.'”
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
According to Macklemore, Sheeran told him that he “doesn’t take sides” on Israel’s genocide in Gaza or its occupation of the Palestinian territories.
Kraft, who is a Jewish-American and passionate advocate of Israel, once led a group of hall of famer American footballers on a tour of Israel, in which he met Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Speaking in Israel in 2019, Kraft told the audience: “After my family, there is nothing I’m more passionate about than the State of Israel and my Jewish identity.”
In 2024, Kraft also withdrew his support from Columbia University after pro-Palestinian demonstrations against Israel's genocide were allowed to happen, saying it was “no longer an institution I recognise".
'The victims are the Palestinian people'
The campaign to silence Macklemore followed his appearances at Ed Sheeran’s MetLife Stadium shows in New Jersey last week, where he told the crowds that he wanted the people of Gaza and the West Bank to know that their plight at the hands of Israel had not been forgotten.
Macklemore, 43, whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty, then told the crowd “Free Palestine” and condemned Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and apartheid in the occupied West Bank.
He was received with cheers from large sections of the crowd but indirectly subjected Sheeran, known for his play-by-the-book apolitical persona, to attacks by the pro-Israel right.
Numerous humanitarian groups and a United Nations commission have said Israel is carrying out a genocide in Gaza.
Israel also faces a genocide case at the International Court of Justice over its onslaught in Gaza.
The International Criminal Court has also issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza.
In his Instagram statement, Macklemore said people like Sheeran, whom he has known for more than a decade, were not the victims and had choices.
"We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families," Macklemore wrote.
"The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence.
"More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don't lose sight of that," he said.
In his own statement, Kraft did not deny that he had corralled other wealthy stadium owners to threaten Sheeran and silence Macklemore.
He said his decision was based on Macklemore’s “recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey… that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.”

deduped_items.body_text:
Palestinian citizens of Israel mobilise against settler outpost in Galilee
Palestinian citizens of Israel have begun daily protests against an outpost established by settlers from the occupied West Bank in the heart of a Palestinian-majority town in the Galilee.
A group of Israelis reportedly from the Tekoa settlement near Bethlehem set up tents on state land in Majd al-Krum, in northern Israel, on Friday.
The town is home mostly to Palestinian citizens of Israel.
The outpost was established after Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced an election campaign plan to “Judaise” the Negev and Galilee by bringing one million additional Jewish residents to the areas.
Smotrich said he wanted to extend the settlement “revolution” from the occupied West Bank to areas inside Israel, where most Palestinian citizens of Israel live.
Majd al-Krum’s local council said the outpost had emerged within “a dangerous political context” and warned that it was intended to create a new reality on the ground.
Izz al-Din Badran, an activist with Majd al-Krum’s popular committee, said residents discovered the outpost on Friday.
The committee subsequently called on residents to maintain an ongoing mobilisation to push the settlers out.

deduped_items.summary: Over 130 lawyers warn UK sanctions on Israeli settlements don't go far enough More than 130 lawyers, former judges and legal academics have warned British Prime Minister Andy Burnham that sanctions announced last week by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband against Israeli settlements fail to meet the UK’s obligations under international law. In a six-page letter sent to Burnham on Tuesday, the lawyers welcome the government’s decision to act alongside Canada and France, but state that “the action cove
deduped_items.body_text:
Over 130 lawyers warn UK sanctions on Israeli settlements don't go far enough
More than 130 lawyers, former judges and legal academics have warned British Prime Minister Andy Burnham that sanctions announced last week by Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband against Israeli settlements fail to meet the UK’s obligations under international law.
In a six-page letter sent to Burnham on Tuesday, the lawyers welcome the government’s decision to act alongside Canada and France, but state that “the action covered in the recent announcement falls far short” of Britain’s obligations to oppose Israel’s occupation of Palestinian territory under a 2024 International Court of Justice ruling.
As part of last week’s announcement, the UK declared that the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territory was illegal. Miliband told parliament that he agrees ethnic cleansing of Palestinians is taking place in the West Bank.
Government sources confirmed to MEE that Israeli settlements in the Golan Heights and in East Jerusalem will be also covered by the UK's new measures, as well as those in the occupied West Bank.
Eleven other countries - Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Iceland, Ireland, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Spain and Sweden - joined the UK in supporting or considering sanctions on trade in goods with settlements.
deduped_items.normalised_title: over 130 lawyers warn uk sanctions on israeli settlements dont go far enough

deduped_items.title: Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour
deduped_items.summary: Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour Submitted by Elis Gjevori on Tue, 09/15/2026 - 12:35 New England Patriots owner rallied other stadium owners against rapper after he condemned Israel’s genocide of Palestinians Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots, on the field during practice prior to Super Bowl LX at Stanford Stadium on 4 February 2026 in Stanford, California Off In a statement shared on Instagram, US rapper Macklemore confirmed
deduped_items.body_text:
Pro-Israel billionaire Robert Kraft led campaign to drop Macklemore from Ed Sheeran tour
In a statement shared on Instagram, US rapper Macklemore confirmed that “Ed Sheeran and his team” had dropped him from the tour after he said “Free Palestine”.
The campaign to remove Macklemore from the tour was driven by billionaire Robert Kraft, owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, who threatened to block Sheeran and his team from using his stadium.
Kraft also rallied other stadium owners across the country to stop the tour from proceeding.
“Ed told me that Kraft said I would not be allowed to perform in his stadium,” Macklemore wrote.
“Ed also told me that Kraft had rallied some of the other stadium owners and collectively they gave him an ultimatum: 'If Macklemore stays on the tour, you will not be allowed to play in our venues.'”
New MEE newsletter: Jerusalem Dispatch
Sign up to get the latest insights and analysis on Israel-Palestine, alongside Turkey Unpacked and other MEE newsletters
According to Macklemore, Sheeran told him that he “doesn’t take sides” on Israel’s genocide in Gaza or its occupation of the Palestinian territories.
Kraft, who is a Jewish-American and passionate advocate of Israel, once led a group of hall of famer American footballers on a tour of Israel, in which he met Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
Speaking in Israel in 2019, Kraft told the audience: “After my family, there is nothing I’m more passionate about than the State of Israel and my Jewish identity.”
In 2024, Kraft also withdrew his support from Columbia University after pro-Palestinian demonstrations against Israel's genocide were allowed to happen, saying it was “no longer an institution I recognise".
'The victims are the Palestinian people'
The campaign to silence Macklemore followed his appearances at Ed Sheeran’s MetLife Stadium shows in New Jersey last week, where he told the crowds that he wanted the people of Gaza and the West Bank to know that their plight at the hands of Israel had not been forgotten.
Macklemore, 43, whose real name is Benjamin Haggerty, then told the crowd “Free Palestine” and condemned Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza and apartheid in the occupied West Bank.
He was received with cheers from large sections of the crowd but indirectly subjected Sheeran, known for his play-by-the-book apolitical persona, to attacks by the pro-Israel right.
Numerous humanitarian groups and a United Nations commission have said Israel is carrying out a genocide in Gaza.
Israel also faces a genocide case at the International Court of Justice over its onslaught in Gaza.
The International Criminal Court has also issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant for war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza.
In his Instagram statement, Macklemore said people like Sheeran, whom he has known for more than a decade, were not the victims and had choices.
"We have careers, money, opportunities, safety and audiences around the world. Whatever consequences any of us face for what we say, we get to go home to our families," Macklemore wrote.
"The victims are the Palestinian people. The men, women and children who have been killed, starved, displaced and forced to live through unimaginable violence.
"More than 20,000 children have been killed in Gaza alone. People are being killed today, and people will be killed tomorrow. I want to make sure that as I tell this story, we don't lose sight of that," he said.
In his own statement, Kraft did not deny that he had corralled other wealthy stadium owners to threaten Sheeran and silence Macklemore.
He said his decision was based on Macklemore’s “recent actions, material shared from the stage during Ed Sheeran’s shows in New Jersey… that we believe has been deeply offensive and hurtful to the Jewish community.”
“I would welcome the opportunity to sit down with Macklemore and discuss the facts,” added Kraft, saying that his

deduped_items.summary: عند مصادقة مجلس النواب الإسباني الخميس على مشروع قانون يفتح الباب أمام منح الجنسية الإسبانية لصحراويين وُلدوا بالصحراء الغربية قبل الـ29 من سبتمبر/ أيلول 1977، في خطوة وصفت بأنها تاريخية. هذا القرار يعيد إلى الواجهة إرث إسبانيا الاستعماري في الإقليم، ويثير في الوقت نفسه أسئلة سياسية بشأن تداعياته على علاقاتها مع المغرب. لمناقشة الموضوع، يشارك في الحلقة: من إسبانيا البشير محمد لحسن الباحث في الإعلام بجامعة إشبيلية، ومن المغرب طارق أتلاتي رئيس المركز المغربي للأبحاث والدراسات الاستراتيجية وأستاذ ا

deduped_items.summary: عند مصادقة مجلس النواب الإسباني الخميس على مشروع قانون يفتح الباب أمام منح الجنسية الإسبانية لصحراويين وُلدوا بالصحراء الغربية قبل الـ29 من سبتمبر/ أيلول 1977، في خطوة وصفت بأنها تاريخية. هذا القرار يعيد إلى الواجهة إرث إسبانيا الاستعماري في الإقليم، ويثير في الوقت نفسه أسئلة سياسية بشأن تداعياته على علاقاتها مع المغرب. لمناقشة الموضوع، يشارك في الحلقة: من إسبانيا البشير محمد لحسن الباحث في الإعلام بجامعة إشبيلية، ومن المغرب طارق أتلاتي رئيس المركز المغربي للأبحاث والدراسات الاستراتيجية وأستاذ ا

deduped_items.summary: في رياضة 24: نبدأ من بطولة أمريكا المفتوحة للتنس، حيث توجت الكازاخستانية إيلينا ريباكينا باللقب على حساب أرينا سابلينكا، لتخطف صدارة التصنيف العالمي وتحرز ثالث ألقابها في الغران سلام، فيما ظفر الألماني ألكسندر زفيريف بلقب الرجال بعد فوزه على الأمريكي بين شيلتون، ليضيف ثاني تتويج له في البطولات الكبرى بعد رولان غاروس. في دوري أبطال أفريقيا، شبيبة الساورة الجزائري يغادر من الدور التمهيدي الأول مقابل تأهل 11 ناديا عربيا إلى الدور المقبل. الدوري الإنكليزي: مانشستر سيتي يفوز على يونايتد بهدف مثير للج

deduped_items.summary: Donald Trump rechazó los llamados a frenar el desarrollo de la inteligencia artificial, calificando las advertencias de “fuerzas negativas” y denunciando una supuesta conspiración que, según él, solo beneficiaría a China. Su postura contrasta con la de líderes tecnológicos que piden ralentizar su avance para mitigar riesgos. Rodolfo Tesone, abogado especialista en inteligencia artificial (IA), presidente emérito y fundador de ENATIC (Asociación Española de la Abogacía y el Derecho Digital), abor

It also released the second part – concerning ad limina visits – of the Final Report of Study Group No. 7 on certain aspects of the figure and ministry of the bishop from a synodal and missionary perspective. deduped_items.title: For these Midwest farmers, regenerative agriculture is about more than soil health. It’s spiritual
deduped_items.summary: NORTHFIELD, Minn. (AP) — Their shared motivation comes amid rising interest in nature-based spirituality and related societal shifts: a rethinking of modern agriculture, growing secularization, climate change anxiety and intensifying interest in health and wellness.
